properties.name: Guge Kingdom — Tsaparang
properties.subtitle: Ngari Prefecture, Tibet, China
properties.claim: A honeycombed cliff city of hundreds of chambers and tunnels, abandoned and depopulated so completely that its fate was forgotten, is presented as a site of mass abduction or a vanished non-human enclave.
properties.context: Guge was a Buddhist kingdom from the 10th century, central to the second transmission of Buddhism into Tibet. Its fall is attributable to the 1630 Ladakhi invasion, recorded in Tibetan and Jesuit sources — António de Andrade's mission was there from 1624. The chambers are cut into soft Zanda-formation clay, and the surviving murals are a major art-historical corpus.
properties.summary: Guge (Tibetan: གུ་གེ་, Wylie: gu ge) was an ancient dynastic kingdom in Western Tibet. The kingdom was centered in present-day Zanda County, Ngari Prefecture, Tibet Autonomous Region. At various points in history after the 10th century AD, the kingdom held sway over a vast area including south-eastern Zanskar, Kinnaur district, and Spiti Valley, either by conquest or as tributaries.
